page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v7 is a Dsv7-family virtual machine configured with 192 vCPUs and 768.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores with Hyper-Threading running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core CPU performance via stress-ng falls in the average tier, multi-core performance is in the top 10% tier, scoring 194,674.5. Memory read bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 14,141.15 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 673.92 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform strongly, with passmark CPU encryption and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both ranking in the top 10%. However, LLM text generation speeds are limited, ranging from weak for small models to average for larger models, despite strong prompt processing speeds enabled by AMX instructions.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D192s_v7 offers high resource density for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio aligns with general-purpose profiles, but the sheer scale of 192 dedicated vCPUs makes it highly effective for massive database operations, static web serving, and highly threaded CPU tasks. Appropriate workloads include large-scale Redis deployments, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and parallelized data processing pipelines.
